###### Posted on November 24, 2026


Thanksgiving is the one holiday built around saying thank you, which makes it a natural moment to bring your team together. Whether everyone sits in one office or logs in from different cities, these **Thanksgiving team building activities** help people slow down, connect and recognize each other’s work before the busy end-of-year rush.


We’ve kept our team’s favorite 10 ideas and added 5 new ones that work just as well on camera as in the room. You’ll also find quick answers on planning the day and including remote colleagues.

##


15 Thanksgiving Team Building Activities for Work


### 1. Meditation


A short guided meditation helps people slow down before the holiday rush. The report shows that mindfulness[meditation relieves back pain](https://comparecamp.com/meditation-statistics/) by 30% and lowers blood pressure by 80%. Employees who spend long hours in seats will find meditations useful for their back cramps. Meditation is a go-to[exercise to decrease anxiety](https://www.crunch.com.au/blog/mindset-motivation/how-your-body-works-during-exercise/) and tension if you want an activity that enables your team to connect mind and spirit—in this context. This spiritual synergy positively impacts team bonds and collaborative efforts at work.


### 2. Gratitude cards


Team members can design and disperse ‘thank you cards to one another, outlining what they are grateful for on the cards. It’s an efficient way to boost team morale in the workplace. Research shows that[63% of employees who gain recognition](https://www.apollotechnical.com/employee-recognition-statistics/) are more likely to stay at their jobs for extended periods. If you work in the people and culture department, this activity will help boost your employer’s branding efforts.


### 3. Munch and learn


As the name suggests, employees eat while they learn more about the company or other interesting notable events that occurred in the company’s History or American History. Similarly, it could be an activity that helps team members learn more about themselves. The satisfaction derived from eating and gaining new knowledge about the company improves their perceptions and connection to the company. Generally, when employees perceive that you’re promoting their development, they’ll be encouraged to do better.


### 4. Teamsgiving


Teamsgiving is an effective way to enable teams to bond over a great cause. You can dedicate some hours out of your work schedule to provide items for people in need. Thanksgiving is about appreciating and sharing love and kindness with loved ones, but we need to extend that act of kindness to people we do not know. One way we can contribute to healing the world is by catering to people who cannot meet their needs. As a corporate leader, you can organize teams to head out on different service projects—some teams can sing at a children’s hospital, while others can coordinate sanitation activities or provide supplies for the homeless,


### 5. Match the plate to its owner


The ‘match the plate to its owner’ activity is a great way to inject humor and liveliness into team members. The idea of the activity is to place an image of a meal on a plate and guess the team member that loves to eat that particular meal. The aim is to help team members pay attention to the tiny details that concern them. Some team members have dietary needs or preferences, and such detailed information may not be overt to the team. This activity would challenge team members’ ability to guess correctly and learn new information about themselves.


### 6. Thanksgiving recipe challenge


There are different ways to go about this challenge. However, we’re proposing an inter-team challenge where team members must write all the ingredients and procedures for preparing a thanksgiving dish within a limited time. The goal of the Thanksgiving recipe challenge is to improve the teams’ ability to communicate, remember the recipe, and agree on their outcome will be assessed.


### 7. Networking Spree


Is there any event that doesn’t involve networking? As social beings, teammates need to interact with each other to learn more about each other. Creating activities for team bonding without including a networking session doesn’t sound right. At the same time, you want your networking sessions to feel like something other than regular meetings. You can inject some fun by creating[timed networking sessions](https://inevent.com/en/speed-networking-ai-matchmaking.php) where team members need to learn as much as they can about each other quickly.


### 8. Thanksgiving happy hour


Who doesn’t love a fun happy hour? If you’re looking for ways to refresh your company’s social engagements, consider creative happy hour promotions that bring even more enthusiasm to these team-building moments. Team members can play games, crack jokes, and have drinks and snacks in person and virtually. Indeed, remote teams can partake in fun; team members can have virtual happy hours and organize fun games to engage every team member using engaging video solutions.


### 9. Team decor challenge


Engaging in team decoration activities is a great way to explore your team’s creativity. You can organize a Thanksgiving-themed team decoration challenge and provide rewards for teams with the most creative concepts. The team decor challenge still applies to you if you run a small company. All your teams need is a white-label video solution that allows customizations from scratch. Team members can customize their meeting rooms to include interactive graphics like 3D designs. There is no limit to creativity!


### 10. Virtual Cook-a-thon


A significant part of Thanksgiving is FOOD. Notice this is the second activity that’s food related. The essence of this activity is for team members to showcase their cooking skills. Team members can volunteer to represent their teams in a contest to determine the team with the shortest meal preparation time. Virtual cook-athrons are highly engaging and educative as team members learn how to prepare new dishes.


#### 11. Friendsgiving Potluck Lunch


Ask everyone to bring one dish that means something to them and share the story behind it. A potluck keeps costs low, and the stories often become the best part of the meal.


#### 12. Thanksgiving Trivia with Live Polls


Run five quick rounds of holiday trivia through live polls, with a leaderboard on screen. Office and remote players answer on their phones, so everyone competes on equal terms.


#### 13. Pie Bake-Off


Invite volunteers to bake a pie and let the team vote on the best one in blind tasting. Add a “most creative” category so non-bakers can enter a store-bought pie with a twist.


#### 14. Virtual Gratitude Wall


Create a shared online board where people post a thank-you note to a colleague. Read a few out at the end of the week, and keep the board open so remote staff can join any time.


#### 15. Fall Scavenger Hunt


Hide autumn-themed items around the office, or send remote players a list of things to find at home, and race to complete it in 20 minutes. Mixed teams help people who rarely work together get talking.


##


What Are Good Thanksgiving Work Party Ideas?


Good Thanksgiving work party ideas are simple, inclusive and easy to join: a potluck lunch, a gratitude wall, Thanksgiving trivia, a pie bake-off or a volunteering morning. Choose one main activity that suits your team size and budget, keep it during work hours, and add an online option so remote colleagues can take part.


Planning ahead for December too? Our[office Christmas party ideas](https://inevent.com/blog/marketing/7-timeless-office-christmas-party-ideas.html) cover 25 themes for in-person, virtual and low-budget teams.


##


How Do You Celebrate Thanksgiving With a Remote Team?


To celebrate Thanksgiving with a remote team, pick activities that work on camera, such as trivia with live polls, a virtual gratitude wall, or a cook-along. Keep the session under an hour, schedule it for a time that suits most time zones, and send a small treat or gift card ahead of time.


**Team Tip:** *Send the calendar invite at least a week ahead and hold it before Wednesday. Many people travel on Thanksgiving week, so a Monday or Tuesday lunchtime slot gets the best turnout, in the office and online.*


### Frequently Asked Questions


#### What are Thanksgiving team building activities?


Thanksgiving team-building activities are games, challenges, and shared experiences that bring colleagues together around the holiday. Popular examples include gratitude cards, potluck lunches, volunteering, trivia, and recipe challenges. They give teams a reason to pause, thank each other, and connect before the busy end-of-year season begins.


#### When should you hold a Thanksgiving team activity?


Hold your Thanksgiving team activity in the week before Thanksgiving, ideally Monday to Wednesday, because many people take Thursday and Friday off to travel. A lunchtime slot works best for most offices, and a short afternoon session suits remote and hybrid teams spread across time zones.


#### Do Thanksgiving team activities need a big budget?


No, Thanksgiving team-building activities don’t need a big budget. Gratitude cards, a potluck, a gratitude wall, trivia and a team decor challenge cost very little. Spend what budget you have on food or a small donation to a local charity, which often means more to people than expensive entertainment.


##


Make Gratitude Part of Your Team Culture


The best Thanksgiving team-building activities don’t need to be elaborate. Pick one or two ideas from this list, include everyone, whether they’re in the room or online, and make thanking each other the main event.
